name: International Protection (Asylum Procedure)

qualifying_event.description: A person with a well-founded fear of persecution (refugee status) or facing a real risk of serious harm on return (subsidiary protection), who cannot or does not wish to seek their home country's protection, may apply for international protection with the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (Asylum Division, Regional Directorate of Budapest and Pest County). Since Government Decree 361/2024, a declaration of intent must generally be submitted at a designated embassy before the formal application can proceed.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Fingerprints and photographs (age 14+, checked against EURODAC); personal interview with interpreter assistance.

requirements.blocker_text: Standard procedure is decided within 60 days, including the personal interview (accelerated procedure: 15 days, at the authority's discretion). Dublin-responsibility checks can suspend the procedure for months if another EU state may be responsible. Detention is possible where the applicant's lawful residence depends solely on the pending application: 72 hours initially, extendable to 60 days by court order, 8 months maximum in aggregate. A negative decision may be appealed within the deadline stated in the rejection; a court may annul the decision and order re-examination.

outcome.duration_length: processing typically 60-75+ days (longer under Dublin suspension); recognised refugee status remains valid until citizenship acquisition or lawful withdrawal; subsidiary protection reviewed every 3 years; tolerated status reviewed annually

sources.title: National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (OIF) -- Asylum Procedure: application process, 60/15-day timelines, Dublin suspensions, detention rules, refugee/subsidiary/tolerated/temporary protection categories, appeal process

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Hungary's initial build. Confirmed directly at tier-1. work_rights and study_rights set to 'restricted' as CONSERVATIVE PLACEHOLDERS: the tier-1 factsheet, despite being unusually detailed on procedure, detention, and appeal, explicitly does not address work rights or study rights during processing -- an unusual gap. This should not be read as confirmation that restricted access is guaranteed; it is simply what could be verified. leads_to_pr set false: no path to hu_national_residence_card is stated in the source (unlike some other countries in this dataset where recognised refugee status directly grants permanent residence). leads_to_citizenship kept true because refugee status is described as remaining valid 'until Hungarian citizenship acquisition or withdrawal,' implying the framework anticipates eventual naturalisation via hu_naturalisation's reduced-3-year track (refugees are one of the named reduced-residence categories there), though no accelerated or automatic citizenship link is stated. 'Tolerated status' (residual protection for those who fail both refugee and subsidiary-protection criteria but cannot be removed) and 'temporary protection' (mass-displacement emergency category) exist per the source but are not modelled as separate routes given their narrower, non-standard nature. Hungary's asylum system has been the subject of EU Commission infringement proceedings and ECtHR rulings regarding border/transit-zone practices -- this route models only the tier-1-stated legal procedure, not enforcement practice, and that broader context is noted here rather than asserted as fact within the route's fields.
